name: Salem Visitor's Center
description: The National Park Service's regional visitor center, set in an 1890s armory drill shed. Exhibits and an orientation film introduce Salem Maritime and the wider Essex Heritage area.

name: A&J King Artisan Bakers
description: An acclaimed Central Street bakery and café since 2006, turning out sourdough and country breads, pastries, and breakfast and lunch sandwiches.

name: A&J King Artisan Bakers
description: An acclaimed Central Street bakery and café since 2006, turning out sourdough and country breads, pastries, and breakfast and lunch sandwiches.

name: Dead Horse Beach
description: A restored crescent of sand along Salem Willows facing Beverly Harbor. Its grim name dates to the 1850s, when the remote shore was used to dispose of dead horses.

name: Collins Cove Beach
description: A small, calm neighborhood beach on Collins Cove with views across the water to Beverly. Sheltered shallows and an adjoining playground make it an easygoing local spot for families.

name: Waikiki Beach At Winter Island Park
Salem Willows Beach
description: A small sandy-and-pebble beach tucked into Salem Willows Park, with calm, clear water and harbor views. Swimming is unguarded but it's a beloved warm-weather spot.

name: Notch Brewing
description: A brewery and waterfront beer garden on the South River specializing in Czech- and German-style session lagers, poured from North America's first Czech side-pour taps.

name: Far From The Tree Cider
description: Salem's hard-cider taproom near the train station, pouring flights of locally pressed apple cider in a family- and dog-friendly room.

name: The Red Line Cafe
description: A cozy downtown breakfast-and-lunch café known for pressed paninis, savory crepes, salads, and good coffee, with free Wi-Fi for lingering.

name: Odd Meter Coffee Co.
description: A small, serious downtown coffee bar run by a father-and-son team, pouring single-origin batch brew and craft espresso for the specialty-coffee crowd.

name: Gulu-Gulu Cafe
description: A European-style café and bar on the Essex Street pedestrian mall, pouring Belgian beers and serving crepes and paninis, with live music most nights of the week.

name: Life Alive Organic Cafe
description: The original location of a beloved New England vegetarian café, serving organic grain-and-veggie bowls, wraps, and smoothies on Essex Street.

name: Front Street Coffeehouse
description: A snug downtown coffeehouse since 1996 — organic espresso, teas, and sandwiches in what regulars fondly call 'Salem's living room.'

name: Brew Box
description: A tiny downtown café known for seasonal lattes and house-made treats — breakfast burritos, pop-tarts, and cinnamon rolls — to fuel a morning of sightseeing.

name: Wolf Next Door Coffee
description: An earth-minded neighborhood coffee shop in the historic Derby Street district, with organic coffee, pastries, and breakfast sandwiches, indoors or out.

name: Jaho
description: A Salem-born specialty coffee roaster and café — espresso and tea by day, wine and cocktails by night, with beans roasted just up the road.

name: Jaho
description: A Salem-born specialty coffee roaster and café — espresso and tea by day, wine and cocktails by night, with beans roasted just up the road.

name: Jaho
description: A Salem-born specialty coffee roaster and café — espresso and tea by day, wine and cocktails by night, with beans roasted just up the road.

name: Kakawa Chocolate House
description: A chocolate house beside the Peabody Essex pouring historical drinking-chocolate 'elixirs,' from Mesoamerican to colonial recipes, alongside artisan truffles. Hours are limited.

name: The Merchant at Joshua Ward House
Salem Public Library
description: Salem's public library since 1889, housed in the elegant Italianate mansion of sea captain John Bertram, whose family gave their grand Essex Street home to the city.

name: Pickering Wharf Marina
description: A waterfront village of shops, restaurants, and a working marina, built in the 1970s in eighteenth-century style at the gateway to Salem's historic harbor.

name: Mahi Mahi Harbor Cruises & Private Events
Halloween Museum
description: A year-round, family-friendly museum tracing Halloween's history and pop culture, complete with blacklit 3D rooms and photo-ready tributes to favorite spooky films.

name: Count Orlok's Nightmare Gallery
description: A horror museum of sixty-plus life-size movie monsters, from Dracula to The Exorcist, sculpted by Hollywood effects artists. Cameras stay in your pocket inside the gallery.

name: Salem Witch Museum
description: Salem's most-visited attraction, where a thirteen-scene narrated stage show inside a Gothic former church dramatizes the events of 1692. A second exhibit traces the changing face of the witch.

name: Peabody Essex Museum
description: Rooted in a 1799 sea-captains' society, the Peabody Essex is among America's oldest and finest museums, with world-class Asian and maritime art and a 200-year-old house brought whole from China.

name: Witch Dungeon Museum
description: Actresses reenact a witch-trial scene drawn from the 1692 court records, after which a guide leads you through a recreated dungeon — a theatrical retelling of Salem's darkest year.

name: Salem Museum Of Torture
description: A walk-through gallery of historical punishment devices — the rack, the iron maiden, and more — with life-size displays detailing centuries of grim European justice.

name: Salem Wax Museum & Salem Witch Village
description: Two attractions in one: wax tableaux of Salem's witch-trial and seafaring history, plus a walk-through witch village, steps from the Witch Trials Memorial.

name: International Monster Museum
description: A lantern-lit walk through the world's monsters, cryptids, and folklore creatures, built by international effects artists. Equal parts museum and jump-scare.

name: Witch House
description: The dark, gabled home of trial judge Jonathan Corwin, built around 1675 — the only structure still standing in Salem with direct ties to the 1692 witch trials, now a house museum.

name: Witch History Museum
description: A guided walk past fifteen life-size scenes recreating the 1692 hysteria, from Tituba's kitchen to the gallows. One of Salem's trio of narrated witch-history attractions.

name: The House Of The Seven Gables
description: The 1668 seaside mansion that inspired Hawthorne's novel — among New England's oldest surviving wooden houses, with a secret staircase and the author's birthplace moved onto its grounds.

name: The Lost Museum
description: A theatrical walk through a 'cabinet of oddities' supposedly lost in Salem's great fire of 1914, with living portraits and special effects. A guided, October-only experience.

name: Gallows Hill
description: The hill long assumed to be the witch-trial execution ground, though the hangings in fact took place downhill at Proctor's Ledge. Today it's a neighborhood park with views over the city.

name: Professor Spindlewink's World of Wizardry
description: A family-friendly walk through six fantasy realms, from enchanted forest to dragon's lair, full of hidden, hands-on magic — a wizardly antidote to Salem's scarier stops.

name: New England Pirate Museum
description: A guided romp through a recreated colonial seaport, a boardable pirate ship, and an eighty-foot cave, telling the tales of New England's real buccaneers. Seasonal.

name: Real Pirates Salem
description: A pirate museum built around real treasure from the Whydah, the wrecked ship of pirate 'Black Sam' Bellamy — the world's only authenticated pirate hoard.

name: Frankenstein's Laboratory
description: A mad-scientist haunt beneath the Salem Wax Museum, winding past live actors and animatronics. Its expanded 'Laboratory of Terror' wing adds a longer, more interactive descent.

name: Pioneer Village
description: America's first living-history museum, built in 1930 to recreate a 1630 Puritan settlement — thatched cottages, wigwams, and a blacksmith's forge — in Forest River Park. Seasonal and ticketed.

name: Salem Common
description: The roughly nine-acre green at the heart of the city, a designated militia training field since 1714 and now a tree-lined park ringed by historic homes and centered on its 1926 bandstand.

name: Waterfront Park
description: A small green space along Derby Street's harborfront, a quiet place to take in the boats and water between Salem's busier wharves.

name: Forest River Park
description: A waterfront park with two beaches, a community pool, and harbor-view picnic hills — also home to Pioneer Village, the recreated 1630 Puritan settlement.

name: Winter Island Park
description: A 54-acre former military outpost on Salem Harbor with a beach, boat ramp, and campground, plus the 1871 Fort Pickering Lighthouse and the earthworks of a colonial-era fort.

name: Salem Willows Park
description: A breezy seaside park since 1858, named for its old willow trees, with vintage arcades, a band shell, harbor views, and the popcorn-and-chowder stands of a classic New England amusement grove.

name: Furlong Park
description: A tidy North Salem waterfront playground with a picnic pavilion, dog area, and water views where children can watch the commuter trains roll past across the cove.

name: Palmer Cove Park
description: A neighborhood park in The Point with ball courts, a playing field, community gardens, and waterfront paths — a recently revamped pocket of green beside the harbor.

name: Ledger Restaurant & Bar
description: Upscale progressive New England dining inside an 1818 bank, where the old vault is now a wine room and the teller windows survive as decor.

name: Turner's Seafood
description: Fresh fish and a raw bar in historic Lyceum Hall — the very room where Alexander Graham Bell is said to have given one of his first public telephone demonstrations.

name: Dire Wolf Tavern
description: A saloon-styled tavern on Washington Street serving elevated comfort food and award-winning sushi, with a hidden speakeasy, Hallowed Ground, tucked downstairs.

name: Adriatic Restaurant & Bar
description: A modern Mediterranean restaurant in the old Salem News building, with house-made bread and pasta, brick-oven pizza, and flavors from the Adriatic coast.

name: Red's Sandwich Shop
description: A Salem breakfast institution since 1945, serving classic diner fare from booths and a counter inside the historic London Coffee House, a Revolution-era meeting spot.

name: The Lobster Shanty
description: A cheeky, colorful seafood joint on Artists' Row, famous for its Lobstertini and a no-pretense menu of New England classics, with live music. Open seasonally.

name: Howling Wolf Taqueria
description: A lively taqueria and cocktail bar on Lafayette Street, slinging tacos and margaritas, with plenty of vegan options, in a festive, colorful room.

name: Flying Saucer Pizza Company
description: New York-style pizza in a sci-fi-themed parlor packed with Doctor Who and Star Wars decor, the dough made fresh in-house every day.

name: Bambolina
description: A wood-fired Neapolitan pizzeria on Derby Street that shares its kitchen with a ramen counter, so a blistered pie can come with a bowl of noodles on the side.

name: The Tavern
description: The cozy, oak-paneled tavern inside the historic 1925 Hawthorne Hotel, serving chowder, burgers, and local drafts within view of Salem Common.

name: Settler
description: An intimate, wine-forward small-plates spot with Mediterranean leanings — house sourdough, whipped ricotta, and crudo. Reservations are a good idea.

name: Finz Seafood & Grill
description: A harborfront seafood restaurant and raw bar on Pickering Wharf, serving sustainably minded fish with wide-open views of Salem Harbor.

name: Sea Level Oyster Bar
description: A two-story waterfront seafood spot on Pickering Wharf with a raw bar, harbor views, and a seasonal patio out over the marina.

Salem's oldest surviving public building (1816), presiding over Derby Square. Fans know it as the Hocus Pocus Halloween party hall, where the Sanderson sisters cast their spell on the crowd with 'I Put a Spell on You.'
name: Old Town Hall
Salem Witch Trials Memorial
description: A solemn memorial dedicated in 1992 beside the old Charter Street cemetery, its low granite walls lined with benches naming each 1692 victim and inscribed with their pleas of innocence, cut off mid-sentence in stone.

name: Bewitched Statue of Elizabeth Montgomery
description: A bronze of Elizabeth Montgomery as Samantha from the sitcom Bewitched, perched on her broom beneath a crescent moon. Unveiled by the TV Land network in 2005 in Lappin Park.

name: Ropes Mansion
description: A grand Georgian mansion of about 1727 on Essex Street, with a free formal garden, kept by the Peabody Essex Museum. Fans know its exterior as Allison's house in Hocus Pocus.

name: Roger Conant Statue
description: A cloaked, broad-hatted bronze of Salem's Puritan founder, who led the 1626 settlement at Naumkeag. Brooding atop a boulder near the Common, it's often mistaken for a witch.

name: Custom House
description: The stately 1819 Federal building where duties were levied at the height of Salem's shipping boom. Nathaniel Hawthorne worked here, and it opens the long introduction to his novel The Scarlet Letter.

name: Salem Maritime National Historic Site
description: America's first National Historic Site (1938), preserving the wharves, Custom House, and tall ship that powered Salem's golden age of global sea trade. It was redesignated a National Historical Park in 2025.

name: McIntire Historic District
description: A leafy district of Federal-era mansions named for Salem's own woodcarver and architect Samuel McIntire, with Chestnut Street long counted among the most beautiful streets in America.

name: Nathaniel Hawthorne Statue
description: A seated bronze of Salem's most famous author, sculpted by Bela Lyon Pratt and dedicated in 1925 on Hawthorne Boulevard, near the streets that shaped his dark New England tales.

name: Proctor's Ledge Memorial
description: A quiet semicircular memorial at the foot of Gallows Hill marking the spot, confirmed by researchers in 2016, where nineteen people were hanged in 1692. Each victim's name is carved in stone.

name: Central Wharf
description: An 1780s Salem Maritime wharf once among the port's largest, its vanished warehouse footprint outlined in stone and its surviving brick store now serving as a park information center.

name: Derby House
description: Salem's oldest brick house, built in 1762 by Captain Richard Derby for his son Elias, who would become one of America's first millionaires through the sea trade.

name: Leslie's Retreat Monument
description: Marks the North Bridge site of 1775's 'Leslie's Retreat,' a bloodless standoff where townsfolk turned back British troops hunting hidden cannon, weeks before the shots at Lexington.

name: Vampfangs
description: The only dedicated vampire shop in New England, fitting Salem with custom fangs since 1993 alongside gothic fashion, fragrance, and a curated shelf of metaphysical goods.

name: Mercy Tavern
description: A lively Derby Street gastropub with globe-spanning comfort food and the longest live-music tradition in Salem, with a kitchen that runs late.

name: Witch Mansion
description: An indoor haunted house on Essex Street full of animatronics and illusions, where visitors choose their own scare level. Open select days, and daily through October.

name: Nocturne
description: A 'dark romantic' boutique and independent bookstore opened in 2022, with curated books, artisan perfume, jewelry, and antiques arranged across a warren of atmospheric rooms.

name: Crow Haven Corner
description: Salem's oldest witch shop, opened in 1971 by the city's famous witch Laurie Cabot. Behind its black-and-purple storefront wait spell kits, tarot, crystals, and psychic readings.

name: Hex Old World Witchery
description: Salem's largest witchcraft shop, dealing in 'Old World' herbs, potions, brooms, and candles. Founded by warlock Christian Day, it draws famously long lines come October.

name: The Cauldron Black
description: A serious traditional occult shop near the Common, lined with candles, herbs, and rare spellbooks, with a roster of readers. A favorite of practitioners over souvenir-seekers.

name: Modern Magic
description: A witch-owned shop and teaching studio that pairs magical tools and apparel with classes in the Craft — a place to buy your supplies and learn to use them.

name: Divinations - Psychic Parlor and Learning Center
Immaculate Conception Church - Mary Queen of the Apostles Parish
First Church in Salem, Unitarian Universalist
St Vasilios (Basil) the Great Greek Orthodox Church
Derby Wharf Light Station
description: A small square brick lighthouse from 1871 at the end of half-mile-long Derby Wharf, still flashing over Salem Harbor. The walk out to it is one of the city's finest waterfront strolls.

name: Fort Pickering Lighthouse
description: An 1871 cast-iron lighthouse on Winter Island beside an old harbor fort. Dark for years, it was relit in 1983 and can be reached on foot through the park.

name: Chambers of Terror
description: Salem's longest-running haunted house, founded in 1993, offering a live 'ghoulish guide,' a vampire-led ghost walk, and fireside ghost stories, with frights you can dial up or down.

name: Artist's Row
description: A small brick pedestrian plaza off Derby Square where local artisans sell jewelry, ceramics, and crafts from seasonal stalls, with a bite to eat and public restrooms close at hand.

name: Village Tavern
description: An upbeat American tavern across from the Peabody Essex, with three bars, a deep craft-beer list, locally loved burgers, and a patio.

name: Bit Bar Salem
description: A retro arcade bar on Derby Street pairing classic cabinets and pinball with craft beer and kitchen fare. Twenty-one-plus after dark, and closed Mondays.

name: Friendship Of Salem
description: A 171-foot replica of the 1797 East Indiaman Friendship, berthed at Derby Wharf. The three-masted tall ship recalls the world-spanning voyages that made Salem one of America's richest ports.

name: Blackcraft Coffee
description: A goth-branded coffee bar tucked inside the Blackcraft apparel shop, serving Salem-themed specialty drinks amid the alt-fashion racks.

name: Hauswitch
description: A bright, modern take on the witch shop, stocking candles, crystals, and home goods from independent makers, plus workshops and readings — witchcraft by way of contemporary design.

name: Pentagram: Witchcraft & Magick Shoppe
description: A witch-run shop across from the Witch Trials Memorial, stocked with handmade tools, candles, oils, and jewelry crafted by local witches, with psychic and medium readings on offer.

name: All Souls Lounge
description: A laid-back cocktail lounge known for vintage drinks, gourmet grilled cheese, and what may be the last standing CD jukebox in Salem.

name: The Roof
description: Salem's only open-air rooftop bar, atop the boutique Hotel Salem, with cocktails, tacos, and views over downtown. Open seasonally.
